Alcohol, drugs and driving","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C - Alcohol, drugs and driving (Section 10)
Coverage: printed pages 51-55 [A01]. Pedagogic emphasis only.

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Alcohol weakens judgment that draws on stored experience for new problems [A01].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Vision is the main driving sense and is harmed at 0.02 BAC for each driver [A01].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A80
A single alcoholic drink can already impair the ability to drive a motor vehicle [A80].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Harm starts with the first drink, so the safest choice is not to drive after use [A01].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
Illegal, store-bought, and prescribed drugs plus strong emotions can impair driving [A01].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A02
Under age 21 it is unlawful to buy, hold, or drink alcohol under zero tolerance [A02].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A02
Ages 13 through 20 face license loss of one year then two years for alcohol acts [A02].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A81
A driver younger than twenty-one who has measurable alcohol in the body faces denial of driving privileges for six months on the first offense. A repeat offense within ten years of an earlier denial brings a loss lasting two years or through the twenty-first birthday, with the longer period controlling [A81].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A82
Over 0.05 BAC breaks the law, and 0.04 does so for CDL holders in Utah [A82].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A83
Refusal of the chemical test selected by the officer brings license revocation: eighteen months for a first offense, then thirty-six months for repeat offenses. For someone younger than twenty-one, the first revocation lasts two years or through the twenty-first birthday, whichever lasts longer. A repeat revocation for that younger driver lasts thirty-six months or through that birthday, again using the longer period [A83].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A04
A first DUI brings an 18-month car device term, or three years if under 21 at arrest [A04].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A05
A court-called interdicted person gives up the card and pays a 7.00 admin fee [A05].
Why it matters: pass point.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0065]
